      State of the Economy

           Global Economic Context

               Global growth remains fragile.

              Growth holding up better than expected bu elevated risks persist due to

                     Geopolitical tensions

                  Trade fragmentation

                     Financial vulnerabilities

             The impact of these shocks may still surface with a lag.

             India’s Growth Performance

               Against this backdrop, India’s performance stands out.

            FY26 Estimates ( as per the first Advance Estimates)

                  Real GDP Growth: 7.4%

             GVA Growth: 7.3%

               This reaffirms India’s status of the fastest-growing major economy for the 4th
              consecutive year.





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                                                                   1

Consumption Trends

                Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE):

               Grew by 7.0% in FY26

                  Accounting for 61.5% of GDP (highest since 2012)

                    (FY23 also recorded 61.5 per cent share).

                Drivers of this growth

               Low inflation

                   Stable employment

                    Rising real incomes

                  Strong rural demand - due to strong agricultural performance

                 Improved urban demand was aided by tax rationalisation, indicate broad-based
               demand momentum.

           Investment Trends

               Investment activity strengthened in FY26,

              Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF):

                               It grew by 7.8% in FY26

                  Accounting around 30% of GDP

                Drivers: This momentum was buoyed by

                  Sustained public capex (expenditure)

                    Revival in private corporate investment (evident from corporate
                 announcements_

           Supply-Side Growth Drivers

              Services sector remains the main growth engine

                   Services GVA: 9.3% growth in H1 FY26 (with 9.1% estimated for full FY26_

               This indicates broad-based services expansion.





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                  2

Fiscal Developments: Anchoring Stability Through Credible
      Consolidation


         Fiscal Credibility and Sovereign Ratings

           Government’s prudent fiscal management has strengthened credibility and reinforced
           confidence in India’s macroeconomic and fiscal framework.

            This led to three sovereign credit rating upgrades in 2025

              Morningstar DBRS

            S&P Global Ratings

               Rating and Investment Information (R&I)


       Revenue Strengthening

          Revenue Receipts

                Centre’s revenue receipts strengthened from an average of about 8.5% of GDP in
             FY16–FY20 to 9.2% of GDP in FY25 (PA).





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                3

This improvement was driven by buoyant non-corporate tax collections, rising
                from: 2.4% of GDP (pre-pandemic) to around 3.3% (post-pandemic).

            Direct Tax Base Expansion

             Expanded steadily, with income tax returns filed increased from 6.9 crore in FY22 to
                9.2 crore in FY25.

               Higher return filings reflects

                 Improved compliance in tax administration

                 Growing number of individuals entering the tax net as their incomes rise.

         GST Performance

              Gross GST collections during April–December 2025 stood at ₹17.4 lakh crore

                   Registered a year-on-year growth of 6.7%.

           GST revenue growth is broadly aligned with prevailing nominal GDP growth
                conditions.

               High-frequency indicators also suggest robust transaction volumes, with cumulative
             e-way bill volumes during April-December 2025 growing by 21% YoY.





        Public Expenditure and Investment Push




ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                            4

Central Government Capital Expenditure

                  Effective CAPEX rose

                From an average of 2.7% of GDP (in the pre-pandemic period)to about 3.9%
                  (post-pandemic)

                  Higher 4% of GDP in FY25.

            State Capex Support

              Through Special Assistance to States for Capital Expenditure (SASCI), the Centre
              has incentivised States to maintain capital spending at around 2.4% of GDP in
              FY25.


         Fiscal Deficit and Debt Trends

          Combined fiscal deficit of State Governments

              Stayed broadly stable at around 2.8% of GDP in the post-pandemic period, similar
                 to pre-pandemic levels

               But it has edged up in recent years to 3.2% in FY25, reflecting emerging pressures
             on State finances.

            Public Debt Position

              General government debt-to-GDP ratio was reduced by about 7.1 percentage
                points since 2020, even while maintaining high public investment.


     Monetary Management & Financial Intermediation


        Overall Sector Performance

             India's monetary and financial sectors have exhibited robust performance in FY26
           (April-December 2025)

                    It is underpinned by strategic policy actions and structural resilience across financial
            intermediation channels.


       Banking Sector Performance

             Significant improvement observed in the asset quality of scheduled commercial banks
           (SCBs), as evidenced by their




ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                  5

GNPA Ratio standing 2.2% (September 2025) reached Multi-decadal low

              Net NPA Ratio: 0.5% (September 2025) reached Record low


        Credit Growth (As of 31 December 2025)

           Year-on-year growth in outstanding credit by SCBs: Increased to 14.5% compared to
           11.2% in December 2024.


         Financial Inclusion Expansion

          Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched in 2014

            Opened 55.02 crore accounts as of March 2025, with 36.63 crore in rural and semi-
              urban areas,

              Helped in establishing foundational savings and transaction infrastructure for
                previously unbanked populations.

          Stand-Up India

               Offers bank loans ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for establishing greenfield
                enterprises

              Targeted Beneficiaries: SC, ST, and women entrepreneurs.

        PM Street Vendor's Aatmanirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme

               Provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors.

          Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)

                Financing micro and small enterprises in manufacturing, trading, services, and
                   allied agricultural activities.

               Disbursed over ₹36.18 lakh crore (till October 2025) across 55.45 crore loan
               accounts.


        Capital Markets & Retail Participation

         Demat Accounts

               During FY26 (till December 2025), 235 lakh of demat accounts were added,
              pushing the total count beyond 21.6 crore.

             Key milestone was the crossing of the 12-crore mark for unique investors in
             September 2025, with nearly a fourth of them being women.





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                6

Mutual Fund Industry

              Expanded, with 5.9 crore unique investors as of the end of December 2025, of
              which

                   3.5 crore (as of November 2025) were from non-tier-I and tier-II cities,

                   This underscores the diffusion of financial participation beyond traditional urban
                    centres.

        Global Capital Ecosystem Development

              India’s first international financial services centre at GIFT City is creating an enabling
          ecosystem to attract and channel global capital.


        Outlook for Sector: Regulatory Strength & Global Validation

           Systemic rise in regulatory quality has received international validation through the
             Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) conducted jointly by the IMF and World
          Bank in 2025.

           Both reports noted an increasingly resilient, diversified, and inclusive financial system,
            with

                 Total financial sector assets at nearly 187% of GDP in CY 2024

                 Capital markets expanding from 144% of GDP in CY 2017 to 175% in CY 2024.

          The assessments found that banks and NBFCs possess adequate capital buffers even
           under severe stress scenarios.


      External Sector


        Global Trade Position

              India’s share of global merchandise exports nearly doubled from 1% to 1.8% (Between
        CY 2005 & CY 2024)

                Its share of global commercial services exports more than doubled from 2% to 4.3%.

          As per UNCTAD Trade & Development Report 2025:

                 India ranked among the leading economies in trade partner diversification,

                         It ranked 3rd in Global South in trade partner diversification





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                         7

Recorded trade diversity score higher than all Global North economies.


        Export Performance

             India’s total exports (FY25): Reached a record USD 825.3 billion in FY25, registering a
           6.1% year-on-year growth

               Driven primarily by robust growth in services exports.

          Non-petroleum exports: Reached a historic high of USD 374.3 billion in FY25

           Non-petroleum, non-gems and jewellery exports constituted nearly four-fifths of
           aggregate merchandise exports.

           Services exports (FY25): Touched an all-time high of USD 387.6 billion, growing by
          13.6%

               Reinforces India’s position as a global hub for technology and business services.


        External Stability Indicators

             India’s Current Account Deficit (CAD): Stood at around 1.3% of GDP (In Q2 FY26 ),
          compared favourably with several other major economies.

             Remained moderate, supported by strong net inflows from services exports and
               remittances that offset the merchandise trade deficit.

           Remittances: India remained the world’s largest recipient of remittances,

                 Inflows reached USD 135.4 billion in FY25 (supporting stability in the external
                account).

              Share of remittances from advanced economies increased, reflecting a growing
                contribution from skilled and professional workers.

             India’s foreign exchange reserves: Increased to USD 701.4 billion (as of 16 January
           2026).

                         It can provide import cover of about 11 months and covering over 94% of external
                debt, thereby strengthening resilience against external volatility.





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                8

Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): India continued to attract substantial foreign direct
            investment, despite subdued global investment environment

              Gross FDI inflows reached USD 64.7 billion during April-November 2025.

            Greenfield investment announcements: India ranked fourth globally in these
          announcements in 2024, with over 1,000 projects

             Emerged as the largest destination for Greenfield digital investments between
              2020-24.


       Inflation: Tamed and Anchored


          Record Low Inflation Performance

                India recorded the lowest inflation rate since the start of the Consumer Price
              Index (CPI) series.

                   April-Dec ‘25 average headline inflation was at 1.7%.

           Moderation in retail inflation can primarily be attributed to the general disinflationary
            trend in food and fuel prices, which together account for 52.7% of India’s CPI basket.




ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                9

Among major Emerging Markets & Developing Economies (EMDEs), India has
           recorded one of the sharpest declines in headline inflation in 2025 over 2024,

                Decline magnitude around 1.8 percentage points


      Agriculture and Food Management


        Sector Growth Trends

           Livestock sector witnessed strong growth, with GVA rising by nearly 195% (between
          FY15 and FY24)

            Fisheries sector has also performed well, with fish production increased by more than
         140% during 2014-2024, compared to the increase from 2004-14.


        Foodgrain Production Performance

            Estimated to have reached 3,577.3 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) in Agriculture Year (AY)
           2024–25, an increase of 254.3 LMT over the previous year.

                         It was due to good monsoon season

            This growth was driven by higher output of rice, wheat, maize and coarse cereals
           (Shree Anna).





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                                  10

Horticulture Perfomance

           Accounts for about 33% of agricultural GVA

                    It has emerged as a key driver of agricultural growth.

            Horticulture production reached 362.08 million tonnes (MT) in 2024-25, surpassing
            the estimated food grain production of 357.73 MT.


         Agricultural Marketing & Infrastructure Reforms


             Agriculture Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) sub-scheme under ISAM and the Agriculture
             Infrastructure Fund (AIF) being implemented to

              Improve efficiency in agricultural marketing and infrastructure

               Strengthen farm-gate facilities and encourage private sector participation.

            Price discovery has been enhanced through the e-NAM Scheme: Onboarded about
             1.79 crore farmers, 2.72 crore traders and 4,698 FPOs, covering 1,522 mandis across 23
            States and 4 UTs (as of December 2025)





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                                                                  11

Farmers’ incomes are supported through assured MSP for mandated crops and PM-
          KISAN income transfers.

                  In addition, PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PMKMY) provides pension support,
               strengthening farmers’ income security and social protection.

               Since its inception, under PM-KISAN, more than ₹4.09 lakh crore has been released
                 to eligible farmers in 21 instalments.

             Under PMKMY, 24.92 lakh farmers are enrolled as of 31 December 2025.


     Services Sector: From Stability to New Frontiers

            Services’ share in GDP: Rose to 53.6% in H1 FY26

            Services’ share in GVA: Stood at the highest ever - 56.4% - as per FAE of FY26 which
          shows the rising weight of modern, tradable and digitally delivered services

           Services Exports: India is the world’s seventh-largest exporter of services

                 India’s Share in global services trade - more than doubled from 2% in 2005 to
             4.3% in 2024.

            Services sector continues to be the largest recipient of foreign direct investment inflows

              Accounted for an average of 80.2% of total FDI during FY23-FY25, up from 77.7%
                   in the pre-pandemic period (FY16-FY20).


      Industry’s Next Leap - Structural Transformation & Global
      Integration


         Industrial Growth Momentum

             India Industrial GVA growth: Recorded 7.0% (Real) in H1 FY26

                 Indicating industrial activity strengthened in FY26, despite subdued and persistent
                global headwinds.

           Manufacturing Growth accelerated, with GVA expanding 7.72% in Q1 and 9.13% in Q2
           FY26, reflecting structural recovery

           Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes across 14 sectors:

                Attracted over ₹2.0 lakh crore of actual investment, generating





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                                    12

Incremental production/sales exceeding ₹18.7 lakh crore and

                 Over 12.6 lakh jobs as of September 2025.

             India’s innovation performance: Strengthened steadily, with its Global Innovation Index
           rank improving to 38th in 2025 from 66th in 2019.

             India Semiconductor Mission: It has advanced domestic capabilities, with 10
           semiconductor manufacturing and packaging projects approved across 6 States,
             involving about ₹1.60 lakh crore of investment.


     Investment & Infrastructure


          Government’s capital expenditure: Increased nearly 4.2 times, from ₹2.63 lakhcrore in
          FY18 to ₹11.21 lakh crore in FY26 (BE)

                 Effective capital expenditure in FY26 (BE) is ₹15.48 lakh crore, positioning
                 infrastructure as a key growth driver.

            National highway infrastructure: Expanded substantially, with the NH network growing
          by about 60% from 91,287 km (FY14) to 1,46,572 km (FY26, up to December)

               Operational High-Speed Corridors increased nearly ten-fold—from 550 km (FY14)
                 to 5,364 km (FY26, up to December).

           Railway infrastructure continued to expand: Rail network reached 69,439 route km as
            of March 2025,

               Targeted addition of 3,500 km in FY26

              99.1% electrification achieved by October 2025.

            Aviation: India has emerged as the world’s third-largest domestic aviation market, with
            the number of airports increasing from 74 in 2014 to 164 in 2025.

          Power sector: Recorded sustained capacity expansion, with installed capacity rising
           11.6% (y-o-y) to 509.74 GW as of November 2025

             Demand–supply gap declined from 4.2% in FY14 to nil by November 2025

          Power sector reforms: Delivered a historic turnaround, with DISCOMs recording a

                 Positive Profit after Tax (PAT) of ₹2,701 crore in FY25 for the first time,

               Reduction in AT&C losses from 22.62% (FY14) to 15.04% (FY25).





ECONOMIC SURVEY 2025-26                                                                                                                    13

Renewable energy constitutes around 49.83% of total power generation capacity as of
          November 2025

                 India ranking third globally in overall RE and installed solar capacity

            Tele-density reached 86.76%, and 5G services are now available in 99.9% of districts
              in the country.

           Clean Tap Water: Over 81% of rural households have access to clean tap water under
            the Jal Jeevan Mission, as of October 2025.

          Space infrastructure: It has strengthened, with India becoming the fourth nation to
           achieve autonomous satellite docking (SpaDeX), alongside expanded indigenous
            missions and increased private-sector participation.


     Environment & Climate Change

             India continues expanding renewable energy capacity to support climate resilience and
           green growth.

            Total Renewable Capacity Added (FY 2025–26 till 31 Dec 2025):

               38.61 GW installed

           Break-up of Renewable Additions:

               Solar Power: 30.16 GW (major contributor)

            Wind Power: 4.47 GW

             Hydro Power: 3.24 GW

              Bio-Power: 0.03 GW
